note: LRRC7 variants cause autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 77 with ID and autism, and functional differences across LRR and PDZ domains support investigating genotype-phenotype correlations.

evidence.text: A cohort study characterized 33 individuals with heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7 causing intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression, and eating behaviors, noting distinct functional consequences between PDZ domain and LRR domain variants.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: We identify here 33 individuals (one of them previously described) with a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7. The clinical spectrum involves intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression and, in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

evidence.text: Animal and mechanistic models of LRRC7, which causes autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 77, demonstrate utility for establishing genotype-phenotype correlations.

source.title: How Studying Rare Disease Leads to Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Development: Lessons from Nonmammalian Models
